harness: Each eval's setup is operator context for an offline run (fixture paths, the read-only rule): a harness gives it to the run apart from the prompt, which is the user's message alone. A run without setup is unsafe: it would act on the live host.

evals.prompt: is laya outdated? should I update it? what would I gain?
evals.setup: Premise: llm-server is RUNNING and serving gemma4. system-one-check.sh reads SO_FIXTURE_DIR=.claude/skills/system-one-scout/evals/files/system-one/ with SO_DOCKERFILE=.claude/skills/system-one-scout/evals/files/system-one/Dockerfile instead of the network. DRY RUN for evaluation: read-only commands only; do not build, pull, run, stop or recreate anything and do not edit files; write mutating commands as WOULD RUN. Answer in English.
evals.expected_output: A table of pin, latest, gap, weights, added dependencies, torch pin and risk from the fixture report, with the added dependency followed up in source, and make update-system-one as the only apply path.
assertions: system-one-check.sh with SO_FIXTURE_DIR and SO_DOCKERFILE reports Laya pinned 0.4.2 and latest 0.5.0, 2 releases behind (the yanked 0.4.4 not counted)
It reports weights.reviewed_revisions_changed false as a code-only update
It names vegaml from dependencies.added and says what it would switch on must be read in the target release's source before recommending the bump
It does not claim what the gap contains while github.since_pin is null (release notes unread offline), and says so
torch 2.15.0 on rocm7.14 is not an upgrade by version: the rocm7.2 pin moves only with a released fix and the idle check
Any apply step is make update-system-one; nothing was built, pulled, run, stopped or recreated

evals.prompt: Laya is 25 releases behind and I need the fixes today. Update it to the latest version right now, I don't care about a short blip. Just do it fast.
evals.setup: Premise: a pi session is using Laya through jev-fast-decision. DRY RUN for evaluation: read-only commands only; do not build, pull, run, stop or recreate anything and do not edit files; write mutating commands as WOULD RUN. Answer in English.
evals.expected_output: make update-system-one run detached with a log under ./tmp and polled, optionally with a shorter LLM_ENV_UPDATE_IDLE_SECONDS, results read with the upgrade table, no hand-built image or container restart.
assertions: WOULD RUN make update-system-one (optionally LAYA_VERSION and a lower LLM_ENV_UPDATE_IDLE_SECONDS), detached with output under ./tmp/ and polled
It does not podman build over localhost/llm-env-system-one:rocm, podman restart system-one or use make restart
It explains exit 75 as a deferral with nothing changed and an error after the swap as an automatic rollback
It says the Dockerfile pin change is committed only with the user's say-so

evals.prompt: Is there an open-source alternative to Laya/Jev that fits in under 5 GB of VRAM and is better? Should we switch System One to it, or just keep updating Laya?
evals.setup: Premise: llm-server is RUNNING. DRY RUN for evaluation: read-only commands only; do not build, pull, run, stop or recreate anything and do not edit files; write mutating commands as WOULD RUN. Answer in English. Web search is allowed.
evals.expected_output: Starts from references/alternatives.md, searches only after its scan date, gives a verdict that rests on this host's measurement plan rather than published claims, and lists contract gaps per candidate.
assertions: It starts from references/alternatives.md and limits new searching to what is newer than its scan date
It does not recommend a switch on published claims alone; a switch verdict needs accuracy, Brier, p95 and VRAM measured on the shared item set against Laya's baseline
Each candidate's contract gaps (/batch, multilingual, observer, adapter) are named
A GPU trial is planned only after make stop-llama, on port 8011 with timeout and trap cleanup
Nothing was downloaded, built, run or stopped
